source_analysis.skill: Form the augmented matrix of a nonsingular 2x2 system, normalize the first pivot, eliminate the lower-left entry, normalize the second pivot, and when requested back-substitute.
reasoning_steps: Translate both equations to augmented rows in x,y order.
Divide row 1 by its nonzero first coefficient.
Subtract the appropriate multiple of row 1 from row 2.
Divide row 2 by the remaining nonzero pivot.
For solve prompts, infer y and back-substitute for x; select the complete correct matrix/solution choice.
invariants: Two equations, two variables; nonsingular coefficient matrix and nonzero first pivot; no row exchange or singular-system classification taught here.
Standard forward elimination with unit pivots, keeping first-row y coefficient; REF is not unique but the stipulated standard procedure determines the displayed result.
Matrix choices must encode row-equivalent systems; solve choices must also give consistent x,y.
Difficulty retains comparable arithmetic workload; easy examples normalize integrally.
permitted_variations: Vary coefficients, constants, signs and zero/nonzero solution coordinates while preserving nonsingularity and manageable arithmetic.
Vary whether first/second pivot normalization is needed and elimination multiplier sign.
Vary correct option position, distractor ordering and relative numerical ranks. Source correct y=-2 frequency is incidental, not a task constraint.
Both REF-only and solve targets are evidenced, with matching prompt, option type and solution endpoint.
source_refs: tutorial ee4b134d-2908-5930-86bb-32537e0d8347: "The row echelon form of a matrix is not unique"; unit diagonal makes back substitution easier.
